use_case_summary: Primary workload: customer support conversational assistant (chat) + fast document search for KB/reranking. Peak concurrency around product launches; sustained daytime throughput for support queues. Must keep sub-200ms token latency for live agent assist; embeddings/retrieval pipelines tolerate up to 2s indexing latency.
poc_notes: Started with Hosted API to reduce onboarding friction — quick wins on chat latency and developer SDKs
Dedicated POC focused on: 1) consistent tail latencies, 2) cost predictability under sustained traffic, 3) integration with their KMS
Benchmarks: Dedicated (4x reserved GPUs) reduced p95 generation latency from 420ms -> 180ms on 1k token sequences in our test harness
Observed token cost with KV cache on: ~35% reduction for support conversation flows during POC
pricing_discussion: Redwood proposal v2: 12-month commit, 3 tier options (base, growth, enterprise). Base = 8k GPU-hours/month reserved; Growth = 16k; Enterprise = 32k
Burst: +50% burst allowance billed at discounted burst rate for up to 10% of months; additional burst billed at overage rate
Overage: capped per-month percentage (proposed 40%) with negotiated cap on unit price (no more than 1.5x list rate), customer wants hard cap
Ramp schedule: 3-month ramp: 50% commit months 1-2, 100% month 3; Redwood accepts phased ramp with pro-rated commit credits
Credits/commit tradeoffs: added option for unused commit credits to roll into next quarter (limited) if annual contract
security_and_compliance_notes: Requires SSO/SAML integration with Okta (Priya coordinating), SOC2 evidence required for procurement
Must have audit logs for all requests retained 90 days minimum, legal pushing for 1 year for some teams
KMS: require customer-managed keys (HSM) for model artifacts and logs. Redwood provided integration doc; technical session scheduled
Data residency: prod traffic in us-east-1; needs confirmation of non-replication to other regions
quotes_from_cx: "We need a predictable monthly spend for capacity — surge events can't blow up our ops budget." — VP Eng (Mark Elliot)
